children: FCNR, ECB and OFCB inflows of $136 billion have materially improved deposit availability for banks, helping lower the credit-deposit (CD) ratio and cost of funds, Kotak Institutional Equities said. The near-term impact, however, is likely to be a 10-30 basis-point compression in net interest margins (NIM), as these "high-quality, regulatory-efficient liabilities" take time to be deployed.
"We are likely to see faster growth in NII, as the benefit is likely to come from asset mix and lower cost of funds," Kotak said.

The industry has mobilised $127 billion through FCNR(B) deposits, around 5% of deposits, and another $9 billion through OFCB and ECB instruments. "Foreign banks appear to have garnered disproportionately higher inflows relative to their balance-sheet size," although private and public sector banks have also participated meaningfully, the brokerage said.

As of August 14, system loan growth stood at 18% y-o-y versus deposit growth of 15%, with the CD ratio declining around 200 bps from its recent peak to 82%. With another $75 billion of inflows in the last fortnight, Kotak expects the CD ratio to moderate further as deposit growth converges towards loan growth.

Kotak said discussions have now shifted to deployment and earnings implications. While FCNR deposits have a finite tenor, primarily three to five years, they are "high-quality liabilities that are SLR, CRR, LCR and PSL efficient, making them valuable for banks".
Banks have three deployment levers: accelerating loan growth, parking surplus liquidity in short-duration instruments before redeploying it into loans, or retiring higher-cost borrowings.

"Earnings accretion is maximized when these deposits are fully deployed into loans, followed by repayment of wholesale borrowings, and lastly when surplus funds remain invested in low-yielding instruments," Kotak said.

The brokerage expects NIMs to have "found its bottom for the industry" after the P&L absorbs the full impact of FCNR deposits over the next two quarters. It expects loan growth to slow as wholesale demand tapers, while FCNR deposits could ease interest rates as banks use them to repay high-cost deposits.

title: FCNR inflows ease funding pressure; NIM may compress 10-30 bps: Kotak
